audit.whatIsWrong: win[] gave Gwen levels 3, 4-5 and first item and gave Aurora level 1, while whys[0] calls level 1 even and whys[2], whys[3] and whys[5] all describe Aurora poking freely with no Gwen answer.
audit.why: Twofold Hex (900 range) and The Weirding (825) both out-range Snip Snip!'s 450 cone, and Across the Veil punishes the Skip 'n Slash entry. Gwen has no answer until Riftmaker plus a second item. A 44.4% win rate over 277 games is not a lane Gwen wins at three stages.
audit.corrected: Skill / Aurora / Aurora / Aurora / Aurora / Aurora / Gwen.

audit.whatIsWrong: No cooldowns anywhere, and the level-6 spike was attributed to an ability that does not exist.
audit.why: Between Worlds is 140/120/100s and Across the Veil 22/21/20/19/18s against Gwen's 22s Hallowed Mist and 13s Skip 'n Slash. Her blink and your mist come back at the same rate — that symmetry is the whole reason the lane is playable at all, and the page never said it.
audit.corrected: whys[2], whys[4], spikes[1].text and mid now carry the real numbers and the real ultimate name.

audit.whatIsWrong: The Weirding is repeatedly called a root; Across the Veil's invisibility is never mentioned; Spirit Abjuration's healing is never mentioned.
audit.why: Riot's text for The Weirding says it damages and slows before Aurora hops backward — the kit flags are slow and zone, with no hardCC. Across the Veil explicitly makes her invisible on landing, which is why chasing the blink loses you the target rather than just the distance. Spirit Abjuration heals her off spirits exorcised from everything she damages, so her poke pattern is also her sustain pattern.
audit.corrected: Every 'E root' becomes 'E slow'; early and mid now name the invisibility on Across the Veil and Spirit Abjuration's poke-healing.

audit.whatIsWrong: 'a bought anti-heal item' was vague and appeared only in the late paragraph.
audit.why: Spirit Abjuration heals her from every spell and auto that connects, so Grievous Wounds matters from the moment she starts poking, not at two items.
audit.corrected: whys[1] and late now tie Grievous Wounds to Spirit Abjuration specifically.

edits.before: Levels 1-2 are roughly even because neither champion wants to commit — Gwen has no Hallowed Mist value yet and Aurora can't all-in pre-blink-reset, so both just soak XP and last-hit. The problem starts around 3: Aurora pokes with Q echoes from a range Gwen's cone Snip Snip! can't reach, and Gwen's Skip 'n Slash dash is her only way in but Aurora holds her W blink to punish it. Don't throw Skip 'n Slash to chase the poke — you'll dash next to a blink, eat a delayed E root, and trade down. Farm, take the chip, and respect that Aurora out-ranges you until your items come online.
edits.after: Levels 1-2 are roughly even because neither of you wants to commit — you have no Hallowed Mist value yet and Aurora cannot all-in before her blink is online, so both of you soak XP and last-hit. The problem starts around 3: she pokes with Twofold Hex from 900 range that your 450 cone cannot reach, Spirit Abjuration heals the chip straight back off you, and Skip 'n Slash is your only way in — which is exactly what Across the Veil punishes, blinking and turning her invisible as you land. Never dash to chase the poke. Farm, buy Grievous Wounds early, and respect that she out-ranges you until your items land.

edits.before: Levels 4-5 are Gwen's single worst window: she's a melee without enough Hallowed Mist uptime, so every walk-up to a minion is a free Q echo and a delayed E root for Aurora. At 6 it gets worse before it gets better — The Weight of Worlds knocks Gwen off her wave and her W blink keeps Aurora outside the mist, so Needlework volleys and Gwen's ability-healing never get to grind. Only commit if Aurora has already blinked with W: Skip 'n Slash in, drop Hallowed Mist as she casts so her Q and E root whiff, then Needlework to slow the disengage. Otherwise take the safe CS and don't force a fight her mobility wins.
edits.after: Levels 4-5 are your single worst window: you are melee without enough Hallowed Mist uptime, so every walk-up to a minion is a free Twofold Hex and Weirding slow for Aurora. At 6 it gets worse before it gets better — Between Worlds knocks you off your wave and Across the Veil keeps her outside the mist and invisible on landing, so Needlework volleys and your ability-healing never get to grind. Only commit once she has spent Across the Veil: Skip 'n Slash in, drop Hallowed Mist as she casts so her Q and the Weirding slow whiff, then Needlework to slow the disengage. Otherwise take the safe CS.

edits.before: This is the only stretch Gwen genuinely owns. Once Riftmaker and her second item land, Snip Snip!'s %-max-HP magic plus the true-damage center snip and her ability-healing turn any caught fight into a kill — and a bought anti-heal item means if she ever pins Aurora inside the mist, Aurora dies before The Weight of Worlds can reset the fight. But Aurora spends the whole game blinking away from exactly that, so don't expect to corner her on the side lane. Group, force fights where Hallowed Mist swallows her Q echoes and E root, and use Skip 'n Slash's reset to stay glued once her W blink is down. Close it before she out-positions you into the very late game.
edits.after: This is the only stretch you genuinely own. Once Riftmaker and your second item land, Snip Snip!'s %-max-HP magic plus the true-damage center snip and your ability-healing turn any caught fight into a kill — and Grievous Wounds against Spirit Abjuration means that if you ever pin her inside the mist, she dies before Between Worlds can reset the fight. But Aurora spends the whole game blinking away from exactly that, so do not expect to corner her in the side lane. Group, force fights where Hallowed Mist swallows her Twofold Hex and Weirding slow, and use Skip 'n Slash's refund to stay glued once Across the Veil is down.

notes: Two separate fabricated ability names on the same matchup. (1) The full layer calls her key ability 'Twofold Hunt' in 24 fields - her Q is Twofold Hex, and every one of those fields describes an escape/blink, which is Across the Veil (W, 22/21/20/19/18s). Swapped to Across the Veil, since that is what the surrounding sentences actually mean. (2) The content layer calls her ultimate 'The Weight of Worlds' in five places - it is Between Worlds (R, 140/120/100s). Third correction: the page says The Weirding is a 'delayed E root' six times. Riot's text says it damages and slows, then Aurora hops backward - it is not a root, and telling a Gwen she is rooted when she is only slowed will get her to burn Flash she did not need. Fourth: Across the Veil grants invisibility on landing, which the page never says. Fifth: the content block is written in third person about Gwen ('Gwen has no mist value', 'she's a melee'); converted to second person. Level chart disagreed with its own prose at five of seven stages; both layers now read Skill/Aurora/Aurora/Aurora/Aurora/Aurora/Gwen, which also matches the 44.4% win rate.
